chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba narrated to us, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn 'Uqba, from 'Alqama, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:

A Bedouin came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) and claimed seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "O Bedouin, have you not already received that from me in full?" He said: "No." The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said to him: "Then choose someone to judge between us."

So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) went with him, and they sought judgment from a man of Quraysh. The man said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." The Qurayshi man said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." So the Qurayshi man ruled in favor of the Bedouin against the Prophet.

The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) rose up in anger, dragging his cloak, and said: "By Allah, I shall go to one who judges between us by the judgment of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty." So he went with him to seek judgment from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said to the Bedouin: "What do you claim?" He said: "I claim seventy dirhams from him as the price of a she-camel I sold to him." He said: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have already paid him in full." He said to the Bedouin: "What do you say to what the Messenger of Allah says?" He said: "I have not received it." Ali (peace be upon him) said: "O Bedouin, by Allah, I know that the Messenger of Allah has already paid you, but I shall ask you: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: 'I am the master of the children of Adam and I do not boast'?" He said: "Yes." Then Ali struck him with his sword and killed him.

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: "O Ali, why did you kill the Bedouin?" He said: "Because he called you a liar, O Messenger of Allah, and whoever calls you a liar, his blood becomes permissible and his killing becomes obligatory."

The Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family) said: "O Ali, by the One who sent me with the truth as a Prophet, you have not erred in the judgment of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, regarding him, so do not repeat the like of this."
ai.seo_question: What happened when a Bedouin falsely claimed money from the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali judged the case?
ai.summary: A Bedouin claimed seventy dirhams from the Prophet for a she-camel. Despite the Prophet's assertion that he had already paid, the Bedouin denied it. A Qurayshi arbitrator ruled against the Prophet based on the Bedouin's denial. The Prophet then brought the case to Imam Ali, who, after the Bedouin again denied receiving payment while acknowledging the Prophet's truthfulness and status as master of the children of Adam, executed the Bedouin for implicitly calling the Prophet a liar. The Prophet confirmed Ali's judgment was correct according to divine law but advised against repeating such an action. This narration was understood by its original audience as demonstrating Ali's uncompromising defense of prophetic authority and his mastery of divine jurisprudence, in contrast to the Qurayshi judge who applied conventional arbitration without considering the religious implications of denying a Prophet's word.
